description: Williams Fernandes Fontinele and colleagues publish connection-queue experiment results and linked Python code for distributed-generation hosting capacity. The September 2026 archive provides eleven JSON result groups with seeds, baselines, fairness tests and sensitivity settings. The companion repository implements a hybrid memetic algorithm and sequential Newton–Raphson power-flow evaluation on IEEE 33-bus and 69-bus systems. Zenodo data are free under CC BY 4.0; code is MIT. The README requires Python 3.12 and pandapower 3.4 or newer. These materials can compare how project ordering affects accepted generation in network-planning simulations. Coverage is generic benchmark networks, not utility approval rules. Transfer uncertainty remains unknown. Numerical robustness and published performance claims were not independently reproduced. Related catalogue record model-pandapower is a solver dependency, not a duplicate. The separate multi-network study uses different experiments and remains a distinct resource.
